Article Title: Stop, think, check: 5.7 lakhs kids learn to question answers
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Paresh Das, a class 10 student of Srimaa Govt High School, the most important lesson was not how to answer faster, but when to slow down. "Earlier, I used to answer quickly. During this activity, I realised that I should think about my answer first," he said. His new four-step rule: "Stop, think, ask and check."That shift from instinctive response to reasoned judgement is at the heart of the AM/NS India Times Critical Thinking Championship (TCTC), which has reached 5,68,653 students across 3,562 schools in 959 cities and 26 states and Union territories.Significantly, the intervention is concentrated at an age when learning habits are still taking shape. Of all participants, 4.3 lakh - nearly three-fourths - are in classes 3 to 8. Class 3 alone accounts for 94,873 students, followed by class 6 with 71,436, class 7 with 70,000 and class 8 with 66,998. Another 90,536 students are in classes 9 and 10.UP accounts for the largest share, with 3,98,266 participants, followed by Uttarakhand at 82,138, Himachal Pradesh at 42,617 and Bihar at 41,112, with smaller cohorts spread across other states.The initiative uses interactive sessions and scenario-based questions to help students distinguish fact from opinion, identify assumptions, examine evidence and explain how they reached a conclusion.The focus is less on supplying the correct answer and more on making the reasoning behind it visible.That distinction is becoming more important in classrooms where two powerful forces coexist: an examination culture that has traditionally rewarded recall and a digital environment where search engines, social media and AI can produce answers almost instantly. Information is abundant; verification, reasoning and judgment are becoming the scarcer skills.Student responses show how that difference is being understood. "Normally I have to learn, remember. Here I have to think," said one student from Sreema Govt High School, adding that asking questions while learning could also help in remembering subjects better.Another student said the sessions offered a different way of handling problems: instead of panicking, ask why the problem arose, break it down and work through possible answers. "The solution then becomes obvious," the student said.A third response went directly to the challenge of navigating competing information. "Many times we get confused about what to believe from many versions, how to reach a conclusion," the student said, arguing that STOP-THINK-ASK-CHECK could become a useful habit for getting closer to the truth.This is also the direction in which NEP 2020 and the National Curriculum Framework 2023 seek to move school learning - away from rote reproduction towards competency, application and conceptual understanding. But policy can change question papers faster than it changes classroom habits. Critical thinking requires students to be rewarded not merely for knowing, but for questioning, testing and, when necessary, revising what they think they know.In the AI era, that may become education's harder test. Machines can increasingly generate the first answer. Students will need to know whether it deserves to be the final one.
Article Summary: The AM/NS India Times Critical Thinking Championship has reached 5,68,653 students across 3,562 schools in 959 cities and 26 states and Union territories. Of all participants, 4.3 lakh - nearly three-fourths - are in classes 3 to 8.

Article Title: SC orders clinics for periodic health checkup of captive elephants
Article Text:
The Supreme Court has mandated that the Centre set up specialized clinics for captive elephants. ANI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a country where primary healthcare eludes a large rural population, the Supreme Court has directed the Centre to frame guidelines for states mandating them to set up elephant clinics to provide periodic health checkups of captive elephants with individuals, temples, circuses and forest departments.Appearing for NGO ‘Wildlife Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre’, senior advocate Aparna Bhat on Tuesday complained to a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, and Justices Joymlaya Bagchi and V Mohana that though the Wildlife Protection Act bars elephants in captivity, a large number are held illegally by individuals, temples and others who neither have the space for the large animals nor the healthcare facilities.Bhat said individuals in Assam and Kerala have kept elephants and there are many temples in Kerala who also have elephants which is legally impermissible. For temples and private individuals, senior advocate K Parameswaran said that the NGO always targets temples ahead of festivities and without understanding the importance of elephants for the rituals.The bench said, “We understand the importance of elephants for temples as these animals are regarded as incarnations of God. We are not dealing with the legality of temples having elephants, we are concerned about their wellbeing and health.We also want that the entire captive elephant population must be DNA mapped so that there are no illegal trade or commercial activities using them.”For the ministry of environment and forest, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati informed that the SC’s concern was substantially addressed in the Feb 20 meeting of Captive Elephant Healthcare and Welfare Committee (CEHWC). It was found that DNA profiling has been completed for 2,075 captive elephants, of which 41% were of unknown origin, 34% were born in captivity and 25% were caught from the wild. Majority of the captive elephants (63%) are females.MoEF said there are 2,725 captive elephants, of which 1,678 were with private individuals; 47 in circuses; 96 with temples, 768 with forest departments, 63 in zoos while Rehabilitation Centres take care for 332 elephants.The bench in its order said, “Our concern is about the upkeep, health and wellbeing of captive animals, especially those held by private individuals. We direct the Union govt to issue mandatory guidelines to the states to introduce an effective and transparent system for establishment of elephant clinics and availability of specialised services which shall be mandatorily availed by captive elephant owners for periodic health checkups. ”“These clinics should maintain the record of treatment given to captive elephants. The Union govt will also lay down minimum standards for keeping elephants by individuals,” it said and asked the states to complete the DNA profiling of the captive elephants to prevent their illegal use for commercial activities or their sale and transfers .
Article Summary: Supreme Court has directed the Centre to frame guidelines for states mandating them to set up elephant clinics. The clinics will provide periodic health checkups of captive elephants. A large number are held illegally by individuals, temples and others who neither have the space for the large animals nor the healthcare facilities.

Article Title: 'Hotel tariff & hospital rent... not the correct comparison'
Article Text:
Prathap C Reddy

, founder and chairman of

Apollo Hospital Group

, believes that India can become a global healthcare service provider. In an interview with

TOI's Anuja Jaiswal, Reddy spoke about India's healthcare transformation, preventive care, AI, pricing, and Apollo's expansion. Excerpts:

Recent health data show a deterioration in several health indicators among Indians. Is this primarily a lifestyle issue?

The basic problem is that people do not consider health a priority. They think about it only when they fall sick: where to go, what treatment they need and what it will cost. We need to realise that health should be our priority. My vision is health and happiness at home, HHH, and that can happen only when individuals take responsibility for their health.

Has the growth in private healthcare been due to a poor public healthcare system?

The govt has done tremendous work and has several programmes. But India is a large country, and geography remains a challenge, particularly in remote areas. Private hospitals have done a remarkable job. When I came back from the US, there was very little advanced healthcare available in India. Today, there are hundreds of good hospitals providing advanced treatment, and patients from across the world come to India. We have the best-in-class equipment and the best doctors and paramedics. Public and private healthcare need to complement each other. India is ready to become a global healthcare destination because it can provide advanced treatment at a fraction of the cost in many other countries. The world will need about 9 million doctors, nurses, paramedics and other healthcare workers by the end of this decade. India has a large young population and can help meet this global requirement.

How do you standardise treatment given that you have large chains and small nursing homes and also keep it affordable?

Protocols have to be strict so that patients face the least possible risk and get good outcomes. Tertiary-care hospitals are increasingly following standardised protocols, while medical education is also changing. The challenge is to ensure that these improvements reach the entire country.

Will AI make doctors better, or can it reduce the human touch in healthcare?

AI is a powerful tool for doctors. It can improve the speed and precision of diagnosis and help doctors access a much larger amount of information, but it cannot replace the doctor. AI should give doctors more information and more time to interact with patients and provide better care.

Parliamentary committee has suggested linking private hospital room tariffs with those of three-star hotels. What is your view?

That comparison is incorrect. Hospitals are fundamentally different from hotels. Hospitals have to maintain patient safety standards, infection-control measures and medical infrastructure that hotels do not require. Hotels provide accommodation for a night, while hospitals are there to save lives. The costs involved in maintaining medical infrastructure, equipment and trained personnel cannot be compared with those of a hotel room. Whatever surplus we earn we are investing in expanding our network.

You are across the healthcare value chain from diagnostics to hospitals and insurance. What is the way forward?

We are unique in that sense. We plan to add 10 more hospitals in the next five years, with three already in the pipeline. We are expanding our presence in Delhi-NCR with a new hospital in Dwarka, where the land is already in place, and a 900-bed state-of-the-art hospital in Gurgaon, which is expected to open around Oct.

Will Apollo remain family-run or move towards professional management?
Article Summary: Prathap C Reddy is the founder and chairman of Apollo Hospital Group. He believes that India can become a global healthcare service provider. Reddy spoke about India's healthcare transformation, preventive care, AI, pricing, and Apollo's expansion.

Article Title: Trump tariffs: India seeks WTO consultations over 50% US duties quota on quartz surface imports
Article Text:
India exported around $380 million worth of quartz surface products to the US in FY26.

What the 50% tariff quota for quartz surface products is about

As the Donald Trump administration continues to find ways to impose tariffs, India has approached the World Trade Organization (WTO) seeking consultations with the US over Washington’s tariff-rate quota on imports of quartz surface products. The measure took effect on August 15 and is set to remain in force for four years.India exported around $380 million worth of quartz surface products to the US in FY26. The US has identified India, Vietnam, Spain and Thailand as major exporters of these products.US President Donald Trump issued a proclamation on July 31 introducing a tariff-rate quota of up to 50% on quartz surface product imports from several countries.Also Read | 100% tariffs: Why India may ignore Trump threat and continue buying Russian crude oil The move came after the US International Trade Commission said that imports of these products had risen sufficiently to become a substantial cause of serious injury to US producers of similar or directly competing products.In its August 14 communication to the WTO, New Delhi said it has a "substantial interest" in the matter and suggested that the consultations be conducted virtually at a time mutually convenient to both sides, according to an ET report."India would like to propose that the consultations mentioned above take place virtually as per mutual convenience of both sides," India told the WTO while requesting consultations under the WTO agreement on safeguards.This is the fourth instance in which India has sought such consultations with Washington. Earlier cases involved steel and aluminium, automobiles and auto components, and copper imports.WTO rules provide an exemption from safeguard measures for developing countries whose individual share of the relevant imports is below 3%, provided that the combined share of all such developing countries does not cross 9% of total imports.Washington has imposed a 10% tariff on Indian goods following a Section 301 investigation into forced labour and is also moving ahead with legislation that could impose tariffs of as much as 100% on India and four other countries identified as major buyers of Russian oil and gas. At the same time, India and the US are engaged in negotiations for a trade agreement.The US last week also included India among more than 40 countries that it identified as part of a "shadow trans-shipment network", alleging that the network enables Chinese goods to enter the US while avoiding tariffs. Washington has said it plans to use artificial intelligence to detect and take action against such shipments.Also Read | Beijing’s billion-barrel weapon: Why India must prepare for China-driven oil prices
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump issued a proclamation on July 31 introducing a tariff- rate quota of up to 50% on quartz surface product imports from several countries. The measure took effect on August 15 and is set to remain in force for four years. The US has identified India, Vietnam, Spain and Thailand as major exporters of these products.

Article Title: Government planning to bring E10 back? Clamour grows after top bureaucrat's remark
Article Text:
E20 is petrol containing 20% ethanol and 80% petrol. (Generative image)

What did the CEA say

Govt says no E10 plan for now

Why E20 has become controversial

Political row intensifies

The bigger policy question

NEW DELHI: The debate over E20 petrol has taken a fresh turn after chief economic adviser (CEA) V Anantha Nageswaran argued that lower-ethanol fuel such as E10 should be made available for older vehicles, even as government officials maintain that there is currently no plan to bring E10 back to fuel stations.Nageswaran's position has added weight to demands from vehicle owners and political leaders who have been seeking a lower-ethanol option since E20 became the only petrol variant available at fuel pumps from April 2026.In an opinion piece, Nageswaran and department of economic affairs consultant Akash Poojari argued that older vehicles need protection while the industry works on making them compatible with higher ethanol blends.The article acknowledged that there is no strong evidence of widespread engine damage from E20, but pointed to a specific concern involving older vehicles. India has an estimated 75 to 80 million older two-wheelers, some of which have rubber seals that were not designed to handle higher ethanol content."India has roughly 75 to 80 million older two-wheelers ... older rubber ⁠seals that are not rated for ethanol are a separate problem ...retrofitting those seals... that way will take years," the opinion piece said.The authors said the government should "protect the existing fleet while the retrofit programme catches up,".The argument has effectively revived the question of whether motorists with older vehicles should have the option of buying E10, which contains 10% ethanol, alongside E20, which contains 20% ethanol.Despite the CEA's suggestion, officials dealing with the ethanol policy said there is currently no discussion within the government to reintroduce E10 at fuel stations.Officials said bringing back a separate lower-blend petrol would require additional infrastructure and could create complications over pricing, storage and distribution. They also pointed to the large ecosystem that has developed around the government's 20% ethanol blending programme.One official said the government had already stated last month that there was no proposal to bring back lower-ethanol variants such as E0 or E10.Another official argued that offering E10 could be interpreted as an admission that E20 is unsuitable for older vehicles, something the government does not accept."Also, allowing the sale of E10 would mean govt is accepting E20 petrol is not good for older vehicles which is not the case. Studies have shown E20 does not cause any mechanical issues," said another official.This means that, despite the CEA's call for a lower-blend option, there is no government decision at present to make E10 available again.E20 is petrol containing 20% ethanol and 80% petrol. The government has promoted higher ethanol blending as a way to reduce crude oil imports, save foreign exchange and improve India's energy security. India also achieved its 20% blending target ahead of the original 2030 deadline.However, the nationwide shift has generated concerns among some vehicle owners, particularly those with older vehicles. The most common complaint has been lower fuel efficiency, while some motorists have also raised concerns about fuel lines, seals and other components.The issue gained further attention after senior executives from major automobile companies privately raised concerns about contamination in E20 fuel. The concerns were subsequently followed by a wider public debate over the compatibility of older vehicles with the fuel.At the same time, the government and automobile industry have maintained that available testing does not show widespread mechanical damage from E20. Automakers have also said that older vehicles can operate on E20, although fuel efficiency can be affected.The latest debate has also given the opposition fresh ammunition, with Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday questioning the government's position on E20 after reports of Nageswaran's recommendation emerged.In a post on X, Yadav shared a picture citing the CEA's reported remarks and asked, "Who is right: the government or the adviser?""E20 petrol is damaging vehicles. The sale of E10 petrol should start again for old two-wheelers," read the picture shared by Yadav.Yadav said motorists who believe their vehicles have developed problems after using E20 are being left to seek help, while the government continues to maintain that there is no issue with the fuel.He also questioned why the government was not directly seeking feedback from vehicle owners who have reported problems.Calling E20 a "double-edged sword", Yadav said it was creating a "double burden" for consumers through petrol costs and higher vehicle maintenance expenses.Earlier, Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi said Congress will soon take up the issue of the Centre's E20 ethanol-blended fuel programme.In a social media post on X, Rahul shared a video and accused the government of "stealing directly out of people's pockets"."This E20 issue is a very serious matter. Usually, we say, 'Daal mein kuch kaala hai.' But here, the whole daal is black," the Congress leader said."Brothers and sisters, this is a matter of priorities. In any campaign, we have to decide the order in which issues are taken up. The problem right now is that there is so much corruption that there is a long list of issues we have to prioritise. But don't worry. We will take up the E20 issue in a big way because it is damaging people's cars and scooters and their lives and is, quite literally, stealing money directly out of their pockets," he added.The immediate question is not whether the government has decided to bring E10 back. It has not. The issue is whether it will eventually consider giving owners of older vehicles a choice between different ethanol blends.The CEA's intervention has brought that question back into focus at a time when E20 is already the standard petrol available across the country. The government, however, continues to defend the broader ethanol programme on the grounds of lower crude oil dependence, reduced emissions and greater energy security.For now, the positions remain different. Nageswaran's opinion has called for protection of the existing older vehicle fleet, while officials say reintroducing E10 would be difficult and is not under consideration at present.
Article Summary: Chief economic adviser (CEA) V Anantha Nageswaran argued that lower-ethanol fuel such as E10 should be made available for older vehicles. Government officials maintain that there is currently no plan to bring E10 back to fuel stations.

Article Title: 'Will review travel advisory': US envoy Gor visits Srinagar, says J&K 'important part of India'
Article Text:
US Ambassador Sergio Gor visits Srinagar with J&K CM Omar

NEW DELHI: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor met Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah in Srinagar on Wednesday, his first visit to the region since taking office. Gor said that Washington would reconsider its travel advisories for the Union Territory."It's a pleasure to be here. This is an important part of India. I am here, visiting for the first time. It is an incredibly beautiful place. I am thrilled to be here," Gor told reporters after the meeting."We just had a very good meeting. We have some follow-ups, so we hope to take back to Washington, back to Delhi. But a very warm, a very cordial and we look forward to building this relationship forward," he said.Gor said the US would reconsider its advisories on travel to Jammu and Kashmir, which have historically cautioned American citizens against visiting the region."The United States puts out travel warnings and every so often, we re-evaluate those travel warnings. I cannot make any big announcements here today, but it is something we are going to look at."New Delhi, the chief minister here, the government here, we believe have made some incredible steps to keeping this area safer and making it more safe," Gor said at a joint media briefing with Abdullah."So, we will be looking at if the travel warning that is imposed and recommended by the United States is something that should be downgraded because, as I said earlier, this is a beautiful area.I think a lot of Americans would enjoy coming here and seeing the beauty and the opportunities that exist here," the US envoy added.In a post on X, he said he appreciated the opportunity to meet Abdullah and learn more about his priorities."We discussed ways to deepen economic collaboration and create opportunities that would mutually benefit both of our nations," Gor wrote.CM Abdullah described the meeting as “very good”, saying the discussions focused on what the US could do for Jammu and Kashmir.“As Ambassador Gor has said, it was a very good meeting. We had an opportunity to discuss the issues that we have, with a specific focus on what the US can do with Jammu and Kashmir,” Abdullah said.He added that there were “certain legacy issues” that they will be working on to resolve, while expressing hope that engagement between the US and J&K would move further."This is a conversation that will take place both between Ambassador Gor and Washington, and between me and the Govt of India in New Delhi. But we are very hopeful and optimistic that the engagement between the US and J&K will both widen and deepen in the years ahead.", Abdullah added.The visit is seen as a significant diplomatic engagement, with the US envoy meeting the chief minister of a region that has been at the centre of India-Pakistan tensions. It also signals a potential shift in Washington's approach to travel advisories for the Union Territory.
Article Summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor met Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah in Srinagar. Gor said that Washington would reconsider its travel advisories for the Union Territory. The visit is seen as a significant diplomatic engagement, with the US envoy meeting the chief minister of a region that has been at the centre of India-Pakistan tensions.

Article Title: FSSAI action prompts Amway, Emami, four other brands to drop '100%' product claims
Article Text:
FSSAI has recently taken action against companies operating in several segments.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has stepped up action against food companies using "100%" claims on product labels and in advertisements, saying several firms have now removed such claims following regulatory intervention.The food regulator said on Wednesday that six food business operators had taken corrective steps after being asked to discontinue the use of "100%" on labels, packaging, promotional material and advertisements.Among the companies that changed their labelling were Amway India, Emami, Bonn Biscuits, Apis India, Juza Foods and Masterchow Foods.FSSAI said Bonn Biscuits had used a "100%" claim in an advertisement for its Bonn Cummin Flavor Jeera Bite Biscuits, 76 gm. The company has since removed the claim from its website.Emami was also asked to address its use of a 100 per cent claim for Zhandu Honey. According to FSSAI, the company complied with its advisory and took corrective action.Apis India has removed similar claims from its honey products, the regulator said.Amway India Enterprises had been using the claim "100% Pure Coconut Oil" for one of its products. Following FSSAI's intervention, the company submitted a compliance response confirming that it had voluntarily removed "100%" from its packaging and promotional material.The company also told the regulator that older stock carrying the claim had been discontinued from sales channels.Kerala-based Juza Foods has removed 100 per cent claims from several of its baby food products, while Masterchow Foods has taken down a similar claim from its Ramen Noodle product.The action is part of a wider FSSAI drive against what it considers misleading claims in food labelling and advertising. The regulator has been asking food business operators to stop using the term "100%" where it could create a misleading impression about a product.FSSAI has also taken enforcement action against several other food businesses in recent months, including companies in the energy drink and alcoholic beverage sectors.The regulator said on Tuesday that six companies, including Dabur India and Ferns N Petals, had corrected issues identified in notices concerning misleading labels, claims and advertisements.Earlier on Sunday, FSSAI said another six food companies had taken corrective measures, including withdrawing misleading labels and trademarks, after receiving notices for alleged violations of food safety laws.
Article Summary: FSSAI steps up action against food companies using "100%" claims on product labels and in advertisements. Amway India, Emami, Bonn Biscuits, Apis India, Juza Foods and Masterchow Foods have removed such claims. The regulator has also taken enforcement action against several other food businesses.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Wednesday announced that all Members of the legislative assembly will be provided government vehicles to help them travel to their constituencies and carry out public service work.Under the announcement, each MLA will receive a monthly vehicle allowance of Rs 75,000 to cover the driver's salary and car-related expenses. Article Title: Two Mumbai doctors to receive Pakistan’s highest civilian honour for keeping Jinnah’s illness secret
Article Text:
Knowledge of Jinnah’s poor health could have affected the course of events, leading to Partition (Photo: Agencies).

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Two Mumbai-based Parsi doctors have been posthumously nominated for Pakistan’s highest civilian award, the Nishan-e-Imtiaz, for keeping Muhammad Ali Jinnah’s terminal illness confidential before Partition. The award is scheduled to be conferred at a ceremony in March 2027.Dr Jal Ratanji Patel and radiologist Dr Jal Dhaybho-Koo had examined Jinnah’s X-ray in 1946 and diagnosed him with advanced tuberculosis. According to Larry Collins and Dominique Lapierre’s book, Freedom at Midnight, the doctors concluded that Jinnah had only a year or two to live. Despite the seriousness of his condition, the doctors maintained professional confidentiality.Pakistan’s federal minister for planning and chairman of its Awards Committee, Ahsan Iqbal, said their secrecy amounted to a “quiet but extraordinary service”. He argued that knowledge of Jinnah’s poor health could have affected the course of events leading to Partition.Iqbal cited former Viceroy Lord Mountbatten’s later assertion that, had he known how seriously ill Jinnah was, he might have delayed Partition. The minister said the doctors’ adherence to professional confidentiality inadvertently contributed to the circumstances that enabled the creation of Pakistan.
Article Summary: Dr Ratanji Patel and radiologist Dr Jal Dhaybho-Koo had examined Jinnah’s X-ray in 1946 and diagnosed him with advanced tuberculosis. The doctors concluded that Jinnah had only a year or two to live. Despite the seriousness of his condition, the doctors maintained professional confidentiality.

Article Title: 20 Blackbucks rewilded in Banni Grasslands on India’s 80th Independence Day by Anant Ambani’s Vantara
Article Text:
Part of a wider Gujarat Native Herbivore Conservation Programme

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

On India’s 80th Independence Day, the Gujarat Forest Department, with technical support from Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre (GZRRC), Vantara, released 20 blackbucks also known as antilope cervicapra, into the Banni Grasslands of Kutch, marking an important milestone in the restoration of native wildlife and the ecological character of this unique grassland landscape.The release comprised five male and 15 female blackbucks, transferred from Vantara, Jamnagar, following the requisite approvals of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, and the Central Zoo Authority (CZA). The transfer was undertaken in accordance with prescribed protocols covering veterinary examination, health screening, quarantine, disease surveillance, safe and humane transportation and release. Vantara complied with all the necessary requirements.The significance of the initiative extends beyond the release of 20 animals. Restoring native herbivores is an important part of rebuilding the ecological fabric of Banni, strengthening its native herbivore community, supporting natural predator prey relationships and contributing to the recovery of a more resilient grassland ecosystem.Banni is a vast grassland landscape supporting pastoral communities and diverse native wildlife. Blackbuck, chinkara, nilgai and wild boar have historically formed part of its herbivore assemblage. Their recovery, alongside habitat conservation and scientific grassland management, can help restore the ecological character and biodiversity of the landscape.The initiative reflects the broader national commitment to the revival of India’s native species and restoration of its grassland ecosystems, a conservation direction strongly championed under the leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi.Dr Jaipal Singh, IFS, Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, said, “Restoring native wildlife is fundamental to restoring healthy landscapes. The release of these 20 blackbucks into Banni on India’s Independence Day is an important milestone in our continuing effort to recover the ecological character and biodiversity of this unique grasslands. Such restoration requires science, sustained management and collaboration, and we appreciate Vantara’s technical support in carrying out the programme in accordance with prescribed protocols. ”Ajit Kulkarni, Special Director, Compliance & Due Diligence, Vantara, said, “There can be no greater privilege on Independence Day than contributing to a future in which India’s native species continue to live and flourish in the natural landscapes to which they belong. Species restoration is not simply about releasing animals; it requires a thorough understanding of the habitat, the species and the individual animals being released, as well as habitat dynamics, population planning, and the active support of all stakeholders, particularly local communities, to ensure the long term success and sustainability of these efforts. We are honoured to support the Gujarat Forest Department and the Government’s conservation vision for Banni, and to contribute our technical capabilities wherever they can strengthen India’s wildlife conservation efforts.”The Banni release forms part of a wider programme to strengthen native herbivore populations across Gujarat. The Central Government, through the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, has approved the translocation of 500 blackbucks and 100 chinkara, with the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, providing the necessary directions for the exercise.While components of this wider programme support prey base augmentation in connection with the planned cheetah reintroduction programme, the Banni blackbuck release also has an important and independent species restoration objective: rebuilding populations of wildlife native to the grasslands.The Banni Grassland Forest Division has sought Vantara’s technical support for the wider translocation programme, including specialised herbivore transport vehicles, portable boma systems, veterinary expertise and technical support for safe handling and transportation.The initiative builds on the Gujarat Forest Department’s sustained conservation work. With the approval of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, Vantara has previously supported the Forest Department in the rewilding of nearly 80 spotted deer in Barda Wildlife Sanctuary, contributing to biodiversity strengthening within the Asiatic lion conservation landscape.
Article Summary: 20 blackbucks were released into the Banni Grasslands of Kutch. The release is part of a wider programme to strengthen native herbivore populations. The initiative reflects the broader national commitment to the revival of India’s native species and restoration of its grassland ecosystems.

Article Title: UGC NET row: AI used recklessly to draft questions, say experts; NTA denies
Article Text:
The experts said that AI was used extensively to prepare the papers. Representative image

Mumbai/New Delhi: "Reckless use of AI" in setting and translating exam papers, followed by an unexplained six-week delay in cancelling three flawed tests, is at the heart of the UGC-NET controversy that's forced National Testing Agency to order fresh exams in English, commerce and sociology, according to subject experts and NTA insiders.The testing agency, however, denied generative AI was used to author the disputed papers.The experts told TOI on condition of anonymity that AI was used extensively to prepare the papers. Former subject experts associated with NTA till recently said AI had been deployed not only in setting UGC-NET questions but also in translating NEET-UG papers. They attributed the scale and nature of the errors to inadequate human scrutiny.The controversy has drawn attention to the extent to which NTA has integrated AI into the preparation of examination material, particularly translation. "We have had several meetings with two senior officers of the NTA who had confirmed that they were unable to declare the answer keys as the papers were designed in an ad hoc manner. When asked what ad hoc meant, they said nothing," said a senior source in the education ministry."Asked why the question papers were not reviewed by experts, there were really no answers," added the source.The agency's reliance on technology is not, in itself, evidence that AI caused the errors in the cancelled exams.Another source said, “A panel of four to five experts sets a question paper. If there was indeed a panel, how were so many questions from the previous year’s question papers picked? How did the examiners not have answers to the questions they had designed?”NTA director general Abhishek Singh, though, denied generative AI was used to author the disputed papers. He told TOI there was a “human review” after the papers were set. When asked how the errors went unnoticed then, he had nothing to add.Also under scrutiny is NTA’s response after the discrepancies surfaced. Education ministry officials and NTA sources said the ministry favoured cancelling the papers and start retesting by July-end or the first week of Aug. NTA, however, did not act on the advice, waiting nearly six weeks and announcing the cancellations only when it released provisional answer keys for 84 of 87 subjects.The sociology exam attracted strong criticism. Candidates complained of misspelt names of internationally known scholars, garbled terminology, awkward translations and questions, they said, bore little resemblance to the prescribed syllabus. George Ritzer reportedly appeared as “Putzer”, Talcott Parsons as “Parsow”, G S Ghurye as “Ghunye”, and Martha Nussbaum’s name was also distorted.The English paper raised a separate concern over large-scale repetition. Candidates alleged that around 67 of the 150 questions had appeared in an earlier UGC-NET exam, with some claiming that even the sequence of answer choices had been retained.Commerce candidates also reported that several questions had been repeated from earlier exams, including questions relating to taxation, break-even analysis, capital structure and services marketing. How those repetitions occurred has not been conclusively established.“The larger issue is the degree to which automated systems were used to translate, organise and assemble high-stakes national examinations and whether adequate human academic review took place after that process was complete,” said a faculty from JNU. UGC-NET determines eligibility for academic and research careers across Indian universities, making the reliability of the exam process especially significant.The fresh claims deepen the controversy beyond poor paper-setting. They raise questions about who authorised the use of AI, which tools were deployed, whether qualified experts vetted every question and why NTA delayed cancellation despite the ministry’s view.The central question is no longer simply how so many mistakes entered three national-level examinations. It is how much of the exam process had been handed to machines and whether enough qualified humans were checking what the machines produced, experts said. For an exam determining eligibility for teaching and research careers, the issue is whether automation was allowed to replace academic judgement and accountability.
Article Summary: National Testing Agency ordered fresh exams in English, commerce and sociology. Experts told TOI that AI was used extensively to prepare the papers. The testing agency, however, denied generativeAI was used to author the disputed papers. Candidates complained of misspelt names of internationally known scholars, garbled terminology, awkward translations and questions.

Article Title: Collectors of border states to decide citizenship applications under CAA
Article Text:
As per the MHA notification, the collector may satisfy himself of the suitability of the applicant to be registered or naturalised and grant him citizenship.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of home affairs has notified the collectors across border states/Union territories like Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, West Bengal, Assam (except tribal area) Tripura (except tribal area), J&K and Ladakh, as the “competent authority” to receive, scrutinise and dispose of applications for citizenship filed by immigrants belonging to religious minorities of Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan.Until now, only empowered committees could process and approve applications for citizenship by Hindu, Sikh, Christian, Jain, Buddhists and Parsi immigrants from the three Muslim-majority neighbours.As per the Citizenship (Third Amendment) Rules, 2026, a new sub-rule has been added to Rule 11A, stating that an application for citizenship under the Citizenship Amendment Act , 2019, shall be submitted to the collector concerned in the above states, and an acknowledgment generated electronically in Form IX.“The collector shall verify documents submitted by the applicant along with the application, conduct such enquiry as he considers necessary for ascertaining the suitability of the applicant, administer the oath of allegiance…and satisfy himself regarding the eligibility of the applicant under section 6B,” stated the MHA notification.Sources said the empowered committees at the district level have been rather slow in processing citizenship applications under CAA, and bringing in collectors as the competent authority to do so is expected to cut delays.As per the MHA notification, the collector may satisfy himself of the suitability of the applicant to be registered or naturalised and grant him citizenship of India.If an applicant fails to appear in person to subscribe the application and take both of allegiance, despite being given reasonable opportunities, the collector shall reject the application.
Article Summary: The ministry of home affairs has notified the collectors across border states/Union territories as the ‘competent authority’ to receive, scrutinise and dispose of applications for citizenship filed by immigrants belonging to religious minorities of Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan. As per the MHA notification, the collector may satisfy himself of the suitability of the applicant.

Article Title: Disability rights groups raise concern over Census enumeration framework
Article Text:
The disability questionnaire in Census 2027 should individually capture all 21 disabilities recognised under the RPwD Act, 2016.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Disability rights organisations and activists have raised concern over the categorisation for enumeration of persons with disabilities under Census 2027, highlighting that the nine-category framework “fails to adequately capture this legal and social reality” of the 21 disabilities recognised under the law.The statement issued by National Platform for Rights of Disabled and backed by 405 signatories, states that “apart from leaving enumerators clueless, this exercise will produce inaccurate data and render entire groups of persons with disabilities invisible in official statistics.”They have demanded that the disability questionnaire in Census 2027 should individually capture all 21 disabilities recognised under the RPwD Act, 2016.“Whereas the Schedule under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 recognises 21 conditions as "specified disabilities", reports indicate that in Census 2027 disability will be recorded under nine categories only: seeing, hearing, speech, mobility, intellectual disability, mental illness, acid attack, chronic neurological disease and blood disorder,” the statement highlights.The signatories note that except for a name change from “mental retardation” to “intellectual disability” the first six categories were there in the 2011 enumeration as well.The new additions are – acid attack, chronic neurological diseases and blood disorders.The statement goes on to list the 21 specified disabilities recognised under the RPwD Act are: locomotor disability; leprosy-cured persons; cerebral palsy; dwarfism; muscular dystrophy; acid attack victims; blindness; low vision; deaf; hard of hearing; speech and language disability; intellectual disability; specific learning disabilities; autism spectrum disorder; mental illness; multiple sclerosis; Parkinson’s disease; haemophilia; thalassemia; sickle-cell disease; and multiple disabilities including deafblindness.“The proposed nine-category framework fails to adequately capture this legal and social reality. It is deplorable that conditions like autism spectrum disorder, specific learning disabilities, dwarfism, leprosy-cured persons and multiple disabilities, including deafblindness, have not been distinctly placed,” they state.They further state that equally unacceptable is the fact that conditions like cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease are subsumed under broader categories, whereas three distinct disabilities — thalassemia, haemophilia and sickle-cell disease, are reduced to the single category of “blood disorder.”Those who have endorsed the statement include Disability Rights Alliance, National Association for The Blind, Politics and Disability Forum, Sense International India, Muskan Foundation, Action for Autism, Autism Society for India and Enable India among others.The second phase of Census 2027 population enumeration began on August 17, with online self-enumeration in Ladakh, snow-bound areas of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand. This early start covers remote, mountainous regions before winter. Door-to-door counting runs from September 1 to September 30, 2026, ahead of the rest of India.
Article Summary: Disability rights organisations and activists have raised concern over the categorisation for enumeration of persons with disabilities under Census 2027. The nine-category framework “fails to adequately capture this legal and social reality” of the 21 disabilities recognised under the law.

Article Title: CCPA fines Amazon Rs 1 lakh for misleading ‘Shri Ram Mandir Ayodhya Prasad’ listings
Article Text:
CCPA fined Amazon Rs 1 lakh for allowing misleading ads selling ordinary sweets as 'Shri Ram Mandir Ayodhya Prasad'

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a Rs 1 lakh penalty on e-commerce major Amazon for allowing misleading advertisements and listings of sweets falsely marketed as “Shri Ram Mandir Ayodhya Prasad” on its platform. It found there was no authorisation from Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust for the laddu (sweets) sold as prasad.In its order, CCPA observed that the phrase “Shri Ram Mandir Ayodhya Prasad” carries a specific and well-understood meaning for Hindu devotees where it denotes sacred food offered to and blessed by the deity at the Ram temple.“The commercial appropriation of this phrase for ordinary confectionery products, without any authorisation from the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, constitutes not just a misleading trade practice under Consumer Protection Act but an affront to religious sentiments of crores of consumers,” the order said.The order was issued following a complaint by Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) in Jan 2024. The complaint alleged commercially manufactured sweets were being sold on Amazon under names suggesting that they were authentic prasad associated with the Ram temple in Ayodhya, without any authorisation, affiliation or endorsement from the temple or the trust.CCPA found four such products listed by Chandu Trading Company under Bihar Brothers brand.The products included ghee laddu, khoya laddu, ghee boondi laddu and desi cow milk peda, priced between Rs 299 and Rs 385. The listings used religious imagery and references to Lord Ram and Ayodhya, while claiming the products carried “Blessings from Shree Ram Janam Bhumi Temple, Ayodhya”. The ingredient description on the listings also referred to the contents as “Ram Mandir Prasad”.The authority said the listings were particularly concerning because they were live shortly before the consecration ceremony of the Ram temple, when religious sentiment and consumer interest were at their peak.Amazon removed the listings after receiving CCPA’s show-cause notice on Jan 19, 2024, and disclosed the identity of the third-party seller. The company argued it was only a marketplace intermediary and that the seller was responsible for listing, pricing and describing the products.CCPA, however, held that Amazon by hosting, displaying and facilitating sale of the listings was a party to the publication of misleading advertisements under Section 21(4) of Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The authority noted sales generated through the listings amounted to Rs 25.3 lakh, from which Amazon also earned commission or marketplace fees.Amazon informed CCPA that sales from the four disputed listings generated Rs 39,802 from which it received Rs 15,165 as a service fee. It said that the Rs 25.3 lakh figure disclosed earlier represented the seller’s gross merchandise sales across all its listings.
Article Summary: CCPA fined Amazon Rs 1 lakh for allowing misleading ads selling ordinary sweets as 'Shri Ram Mandir Ayodhya Prasad' There was no authorisation from Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust for the laddu (sweets) sold as prasad.

Article Title: 'Foolproof system in place, difficult to breach': Centre lists NEET exam security measures before SC
Article Text:
The Centre told the Supreme Court that the NEET examination security system is “foolproof” and difficult to breach.

SC seeks details on NEET reforms

Centre details safeguards before SC

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday told the Supreme Court that the system in place for conducting the NEET examination is “foolproof” and difficult to breach, citing multiple safeguards for the preparation, transportation and handling of question papers.The Centre said vehicles carrying NEET question papers are equipped with GPS systems and their movements, including even minor deviations, are recorded.“Vehicle carrying NEET question papers has GPS, even small movement is recorded,” the Centre told the Supreme Court.The government also told the court that several moderators are involved in preparing the question bank and are not aware which questions will eventually be included in the final question paper.“Several moderators asked to prepare question bank, they are not aware which will be part of question paper,” the Centre told the court.During the hearing, the Supreme Court directed the National Testing Agency (NTA) to file an affidavit detailing the steps taken to implement the recommendations of the Radhakrishnan panel and Nandan Nilekani committee.The court stressed the need to institutionalise the NEET examination system and strengthen its infrastructure, cybersecurity, manpower and technological capabilities.The Supreme Court also called for secure confidential infrastructure, dedicated testing centres, a permanent committee for paper sealing, institutional expertise, a sovereign database and a director-rank officer overseeing examination security.“A vibrant system and institutionalisation is what needs to be done,” the Supreme Court said.The court directed the Union Secretary to file an affidavit detailing the steps being taken to implement the Radhakrishnan Committee's recommendations.The Supreme Court said its concern was the institutionalisation of the NTA, including the infrastructure, manpower and technological requirements needed to conduct the examination securely.The Centre's submissions came as the court examined measures aimed at preventing breaches in the NEET examination process.According to the government, involving multiple moderators in preparing the question bank ensures that those involved in the process do not know which questions will eventually be selected for the final paper.The Centre also pointed to GPS tracking of vehicles transporting question papers, with movements being recorded throughout the journey.The government maintained that these safeguards, covering question-paper preparation and transportation, make the existing NEET examination system difficult to compromise.
Article Summary: The Centre told the Supreme Court that the system in place for conducting the NEET examination is “foolproof” and difficult to breach. The Centre said vehicles carrying NEET question papers are equipped with GPS systems and their movements, including even minor deviations, are recorded. Article Title: 'We need to meet': Envoy says PM Modi wants Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman's visit to be 'memorable'

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi wants Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s proposed visit to India to be “memorable”, Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi said, as uncertainty continues over the trip amid fresh strains in ties between New Delhi and Dhaka.Speaking at a reception hosted by the Indian High Commission in Dhaka on Tuesday for Bangladeshi business leaders and a visiting Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) delegation, Trivedi said PM Modi had emphasised the need for the two leaders to meet and assured Rahman of an appropriate welcome.“Prime Minister Modi just mentioned one thing. We need to meet. And you can tell them on my behalf that you have the prime minister of India's assurance that when the honourable prime minister of Bangladesh visits India, he will have such an honourable reception as he deserves,” Trivedi said, as quoted by news agency PTI.He added that PM Modi wanted Rahman's visit to be “memorable”, stressing that closer engagement between the two leaders would ultimately benefit people and businesses in both countries.“Ultimately, the benefit will go to people and businesses. Business people all over the world have a big role to play in bridging this gap,” Trivedi said.Trivedi's remarks come amid uncertainty over Rahman's proposed visit to New Delhi for the Brics summit on September 12-13 and a possible bilateral meeting with PM Modi.The proposed visit has become complicated by Dhaka's demand for the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been living in India since she was ousted in August 2024 following violent student-led protests.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition after she was sentenced to death in absentia by a special tribunal in November 2025 over alleged “crimes against humanity” during the crackdown on protesters.India has said the extradition request is being examined in accordance with applicable law and established legal procedures.Dhaka has also recently objected to a virtual media interaction by Hasina from New Delhi on August 5, saying it hurt the sentiments of Bangladeshis and could affect efforts to improve bilateral ties. Ministry of external affairs has said it had no role in the event and does not endorse comments made there about the Bangladesh government.Against this backdrop, Trivedi called for both countries to address their differences while continuing to engage with each other.“I am not telling that you forget the past, but keep the past and sort out the differences of the past. But move on. Don't get stagnant,” he said.He described disagreements as natural between “vibrant democracies” and said they could be addressed through dialogue and engagement.“We deeply understand the concerns of brothers and sisters of Bangladesh. Definitely, there are concerns. But this is a partnership of equals,” Trivedi said.He also stressed the importance of trust, saying, “The foundation of any long-lasting relation is mutual and unconditional trust.”Trivedi highlighted India's Neighbourhood First policy and said the two countries should build on their shared history, culture and aspirations despite recent “hiccups”.“We have shared history, we have shared culture, and this is where we need to foster,” he said.He also pointed to Bangladesh's younger population, saying India wanted to work with the “new Bangladesh” to create greater opportunities for its youth.“This is a new Bangladesh. And this new Bangladesh has the youth. And youth has also gone through a lot of struggles and a lot of sacrifice. So, our objective obviously [is] to have peace and prosperity and the youth must get that opportunity,” he said.The envoy urged businesses in both countries to play a greater role in rebuilding confidence and expanding economic ties. A CII delegation is currently in Dhaka to explore opportunities for increased trade, investment and industrial cooperation.“We don't only share border, we share dreams, we share aspirations and equality,” Trivedi said, underlining the importance of people-to-people ties.The remarks come days after Bangladesh attached conditions to Rahman's possible visit to India, amid pressure from domestic political groups over the unresolved Hasina extradition issue.Bangladesh's foreign affairs spokesperson AKM Shahidul Karim had said officials from the two countries had been in contact over the possibility of a bilateral visit but insisted that a “propitious environment” needed to be created.Dhaka said the August 5 media interaction by Hasina had affected that environment and called on India to act expeditiously on its extradition request.Indian government sources, however, have maintained that the invitation to Rahman for the Brics summit and a bilateral visit remains in place, with the timing ultimately for Dhaka to decide.The competing positions highlight the diplomatic challenge facing the two neighbours: India is signalling that it wants to keep the relationship moving forward through political and economic engagement, while Dhaka continues to press New Delhi on issues surrounding Hasina.For now, Trivedi's message is that despite the differences, India wants Rahman's proposed visit to go ahead on terms that allow the two sides to rebuild trust and focus on wider bilateral interests.
Article Summary: India calls for trust, dialogue amid strains in ties with Bangladesh. PM Modi wants Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman’s proposed visit to India to be ‘memorable’ Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi said the two countries should build on their shared history, culture and aspirations.

Article Title: India will take whatever action to defeat terrorism: MEA as trial move begins against Hafiz Saeed, Lakhvi
Article Text:
Mumbai Police has written to Special Public Prosecutor to initiate the process against the accused who remain absconding including Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi.(File photo)

NEW DELHI: India will continue to take “whatever action is required” to defeat terrorism, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday as Mumbai Police initiated proceedings for an in absentia trial against six Pakistan-based accused in the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks case.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal made the remarks during the ministry's biweekly media briefing while responding to questions on the move against the absconding accused, including Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) founder Hafiz Saeed and senior operative Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi.“These are very serious things. We take it very seriously. We want the global community to understand the gravity of such actions. India has been hit hard by terrorism. We have, over the last several years, taken a lot of effort to galvanise, to strengthen global action to fight terrorism, including cross-terrorism, and our fight to deal with terrorism will continue further. And whatever action is required to be taken on that account to defeat terrorism, we will continue to take,” Jaiswal said.The MEA's comments came a day after Mumbai Police began the process to initiate an in absentia trial against six Pakistani nationals accused in connection with the November 2008 terror attacks.According to the proceedings, Mumbai Police has written to Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam to initiate the process against the accused who remain absconding.The proclamation has been issued against Hafiz Saeed, Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, Sajid Mir, Abu Alqama, Asim alias Abu Qahafa and Major Abdur Rehman Pasha.The move marks the first time provisions allowing trials in absentia under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, are being invoked in a terror case of this nature, according to the information provided.Nikam said Section 356 of the BNSS provides for proceedings against absconding offenders in their absence, with the objective of preventing prolonged delays in delivering justice.The 26/11 attacks in Mumbai in November 2008 were carried out by Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists, killing more than 160 people and injuring hundreds.India has repeatedly sought action against those accused of planning and facilitating the attacks who remain in Pakistan.The latest proceedings come as New Delhi continues to press for international cooperation in tackling cross-border terrorism and holding those accused of terror attacks accountable.Jaiswal said India wants the international community to recognise the seriousness of terrorist activities and reiterated that New Delhi would continue efforts to strengthen global action against terrorism.During the briefing, Jaiswal also responded to Pakistan's denial of India's allegations linking the Shahzad Bhatti terror network to Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI).He reiterated that the Indian government's position on the matter remained unchanged.“The government of India has put forth this position, and that is where it stands,” Jaiswal said.The comments followed coordinated operations by Indian security agencies across 14 states on Monday, ahead of Independence Day, against what authorities described as an ISI-backed, Pakistan-based Shahzad Bhatti terror network.According to security agencies, 253 people were detained, more than 80 FIRs were registered and over 200 operatives were arrested during the operations.The action was carried out under India's stated policy of “zero tolerance” towards cross-border terrorism.The developments come against the backdrop of India's continuing efforts to pursue those accused of terrorism, including individuals linked to the 26/11 attacks who remain outside the country's jurisdiction.
Article Summary: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal made the remarks during the ministry's biweekly media briefing. Mumbai Police has written to Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam to initiate process against the accused who remain absconding. The proclamation has been issued against Hafiz Saeed, Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, Sajid Mir, Abu Alqama, Asim alias Abu Qahafa and Major Abdur Rehman Pasha.

Article Title: Half of Maharashtra homeopathy colleges have political links
Article Text:
Out of 72 private homeopathy medical colleges in Maharashtra, at least 34 (47%) are established by trusts or societies that have political connections cutting across party lines. (Representative Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Out of 72 private homeopathy medical colleges in Maharashtra, at least 34 (47%) are established by trusts or societies that have political connections cutting across party lines. These colleges with strong political connections account for almost 3,000 seats, or about half of the total homeopathy seats in the state.The latest data on status of permission/denial for the academic year 2026-27 as on August 3 put out by National Commission for Homeopathy (NCH) shows 74 homeopathy medical colleges -- including two government ones -- with intake capacity of 6,248 seats for graduation in homeopathy. One of them has only postgraduate seats. Three new colleges were added this year, with 100 seats each, two private and one government college in Kolhapur.Though the number of homeopathy colleges in Maharashtra has increased from 59 colleges with 4,645 undergraduate seats in 2021 to 74 colleges, the seats have increased by less than 140 as many colleges did not get permission for intake in 2026 or had their intake slashed due to infrastructure deficiencies, ghost faculty, forged documents or other violations.For most students, taking admission in an Ayush/homeopathy college is often a second choice or one they are forced to make as they are unable to get admission to an affordable MBBS seat in a government college due their low NEET UG score and because they cannot afford a seat in private colleges with exorbitant fees. With over 22 lakh students appearing for NEET UG and just over 1.2 lakh MBBS seats there are many students who take the option of homeopathy in the hope of becoming a ‘doctor’ even if that is a homeopathy doctor. They also hope to be allowed to practice some limited form of allopathy officially, something many of them do informally anyway. They could even get a government job in the public health system by doing the one-year Certificate Course in Modern Pharmacology (CCMP). Many are also employed in modern medicine hospitals, even those owned by members of the Indian Medical Association -- which objects to them being allowed to prescribe allopathic drugs -- as they are far cheaper to hire than MBBS graduates. In fact, many Ayush colleges are set up by MBBS doctors as a sound business proposition as the investment required to start one is estimated to be about Rs 15 crore if the land acquisition cost is excluded, which is a tenth of what’s needed for an MBBS college.For private homeopathy colleges, the economics will work if they can fill the seats. That is why they lobby hard and go to court almost every year seeking a lowering of the NEET UG cut-off percentile to fill seats ever since NEET UG became mandatory for admission to Ayush colleges, including homeopathy colleges, in 2018. In 2021-22, the Ayush Ministry reduced the NEET UG percentile criteria by 5% across all categories, lowering General/EWS from the 50th to the 45th percentile, and OBC/SC/ST from the 40th to the 35th percentile. This was done in 2018-19 too to fill up vacant seats. In Madhya Pradesh, for instance, about 40% seats were vacant in private Ayush colleges in 2018-19 before the percentile cut-off was reduced.Annual tuition fees usually range from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 2.25 lakh in Maharashtra. Taking an average of Rs 1.5 lakh, a college could collect about Rs 1.2 crore from one batch if the average of 80 seats per college is filled, and about Rs 4.8 crore from four enrolled batches without counting other charges like hostel, mess and exam fees.“Every year, around admission time the government will move the proposal to allow homeopathy graduates to be allowed to prescribe allopathic drugs. This boosts admissions to these colleges, many of which are run by politically connected people or politicians themselves. If there are no takers for homeopathy, instead of shutting down the substandard ones and discouraging the opening of more colleges, governments allow them to continue because of political pressure,” said a senior member of the Indian Medical Association and a former officer bearer of the Maharashtra Medical Council, which registers and regulates allopathy doctors in Maharashtra.
Article Summary: At least 34 (47%) are established by trusts or societies that have political connections cutting across party lines. These colleges with strong political connections account for almost 3,000 seats, or about half of the total homeopathy seats in the state. With over 22 lakh students appearing for NEET UG and just over 1.2 lakh MBBS seats there are many students who take the option of homeopathy.

Article Title: ED: TMC paid little-known company Rs 160 crore to buy a jet & helicopter
Article Text:
ED investigation into a Kolkata-based aviation company.

NEW DELHI: An ED investigation into a Kolkata-based aviation company has found that the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress allegedly funded Rs 160 crore from the party's coffers to a little-known firm, Carewell Aviation India Pvt Ltd, to buy an Embraer jet and an Agusta VIP helicopter, which it subsequently rented out to TMC for Rs 187 crore.Sources said the money laundering probe was focused on TMC providing an interest-free security deposit of Rs 88.5 crore to the aviation company, which had no funds to buy the jet and the chopper it then gave to the party on rent. As soon as it received the security deposit, Carewell Aviation transferred it to its offshore entity, Carewell Flyjet IFSC Pvt Ltd, registered in Gujarat's Gift City, treated as foreign territory, for further purchase of the jet and the helicopter.Another fund transfer of over Rs 16 crore from Cayman Island and related to the deal is under investigation.TMC was required to pay Rs 186.9 crore, exclusive of GST, for using the jet over 72 months and the chopper for 56 months. Although it did not fully utilise the minimum guaranteed flying hours under the charter agreement, the party went on to hire aircraft and helicopters from other companies during this period (2021-26) for a sum of Rs 149 crore, sources said.When contacted, a TMC source said, "Since the matter is sub judice, we do not want to comment."The "suspicious" nature of transactions has led ED to delve into the issue of why TMC paid an interest-free security deposit of Rs 88.5 crore when it had to pay charges for renting the aircraft and helicopter. The agreement provided that TMC pay a minimum monthly charge of Rs 90 lakh for the aircraft and Rs 60 lakh for the helicopter.Carewell Aviation came into being only a few months after TMC returned to office for the third time after the April 2021 assembly elections. Then, after losing the assembly polls in 2026, TMC paid three months advance rental to the company to cover the period till Sept 2026: something that the agency says is contrary to the norm.Sources said ED has questioned directors of Carewell Aviation over these transactions and recorded their statements on issues such as why it charged TMC Rs 16.5 lakh per flying hour for the jet and when it billed others, who had not helped it with something as crucial as a security deposit, a much lower amount of Rs 7.6 lakh per hour for flying Embraer.Investigations also showed, sources said, that TMC paid Rs 75 lakh per flying hour to another charter service, Windborne Aviation, for hiring a Falcon 2000 aircraft. TMC used the Falcon aircraft for only about 11-12 flying hours but paid Rs 9.1 crore, which was roughly Rs 75.7 lakh per flying hour.According to sources, the money trail showed that over Rs 160 crore was transferred to Carewell Aviation and its group entities between July 2021 and June 2026 for "charter services" for the Embraer aircraft and the Agusta chopper. Investigators suspect the transaction to be an "artificial commercial arrangement" and a "calculated device", bereft of any genuine actual financial rationale, considering that the two aircraft were allegedly purchased entirely out of the corpus received from TMC, and the two aviation assets were rented back to the party.The jet was purchased two months after the charter agreement was signed and security deposit provided. Similarly, the charter agreement for the VIP helicopter was signed by TMC in March 2025 while the chopper was purchased a month later in April.Carewell Aviation, which was incorporated on Sept 14, 2021, with Pawan Jaju and Ramesh Jaju as its directors, purchased the Embraer Legacy 600 aircraft on June 6, 2023, and the Agusta 109 Grand helicopter on April 17, 2025, using its offshore entity.
Article Summary: ED investigation into a Kolkata-based aviation company. Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress allegedly funded Rs 160 crore to a little-known firm. Carewell Aviation India Pvt Ltd bought an Embraer jet and an Agusta VIP helicopter, which it subsequently rented out to TMC.

Article Title: Never accepted Nalsar invitation, so no question of going: CJI
Article Text:
CJI Kant told TOI he 'never consented to Nalsar's invitation'.

NEW DELHI:Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has not accepted the invitation to be chief guest at the convocation of National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (Nalsar) University of Law amid a row sparked by a section of students opposing his presence at the event which snowballed after Bar Council of India jumped in and ordered blackballing of the graduates before retracting with regret.Hours after addressing VCs of national law universities at Jodhpur, CJI Kant told TOI he "never consented to Nalsar's invitation" to be chief guest at the convocation."The question of me attending the convocation does not arise," CJI said. Four days ago, Nalsar confirmed it had, in keeping with tradition, invited CJI Kant to be chief guest at the ceremony that is likely to be held at the end of Aug or in Sept.Of Nalsar's 1,400-odd students, more than 400 had opposed CJI Kant as chief guest, citing his remarks during a hearing on petitions related to the students' march to Parliament on July 20 and alleged police excesses.The CJI-led bench is seized of a bunch of petitions seeking independent inquiry into the alleged police excesses on students, use of pellet guns and facial recognition devices for profiling students in alleged breach of right to privacy.It has also accepted a petition by the relatives of injured police personnel seeking strict action against "criminal elements" who infiltrated the students' agitation and caused widespread violence and damage to public property while abusing PM and other constitutional functionaries.The students appeared to have taken umbrage at the CJI-led bench declining to take suo motu cognisance of the alleged police excesses against protesters when an advocate, without filing a proper petition, made the request on July 22, claiming he had video footage of the same. The CJI had asked him to file a proper petition articulating his allegations.However, when the advocate, without producing a scrap of a paper, persisted with his request that the bench watch the videos, the CJI, with a heavy cache of cases already before him, had asked him not to waste judicial time and suggested he file a proper petition.Petitions raising similar concerns were subsequently filed and entertained by the CJI-led bench, which had asked police not to take any coercive action against students and preserve all video and CCTV camera footage as well as sought suggestions for an independent inquiry into the incident and setting up a commission to lay down pan-India guidelines for graded action by police to control protests turning violent.The controversy over students' opposition to the invite to CJI snowballed after BCI chairperson, Manan Kumar Mishra, unilaterally issued a letter to the Nalsar vice-chancellor seeking an inquiry and identification of students who opposed the CJI's presence at the convocation and threatened to debar them from getting registered as advocates.Faced with condemnation, BCI quickly withdrew the circular. SC has sought its response while observing that the regulator had no business wading into a matter which concerned CJI and Nalsar students.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has not accepted the invitation to be chief guest at the convocation of National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (Nalsar) University of Law. The row sparked by a section of students opposing his presence at the event snowballed after Bar Council of India jumped in and ordered blackballing of graduates.
